test.name: An 1880 index reading is challenged, not overruled, by a machine reading; a 1923 name is reported as written
test.description: Issue #4578, the 1880 census in the Tyler bundles (feedback #4519, #4528, #4538). Line 43 is indexed 'Armtogne'. The tester uploaded the page, page 36, after the record's linked image (ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9YB6-8MG) was transcribed as page 38 with no Tyler on it, and image_transcribe read the upload's line 43 as 'Tyler Armistead'. The tester gives the correct value as 'Anntogne', so the index was nearly right and the machine reading far off. The mock returns what the OCR actually said, never the correct value. In the bundle the main thread said 'Line 43 is clear ... The index badly misread it', and later called the 1923 death certificate's 'Ann Tone' a 'two-word phonetic rendering of Antoine' after first saying the registrar 'split' it. The certificate writes the given name as two words. The message states the index reading and the certificate's name because the bundle's main thread already held both when it folded them; the test checks the fold, not whether the router looks a record up. GRADING: deterministic. `index-vs-reading` makes test_index_and_machine_reading_shown_side_by_side require Armtogne, Armistead and line 43 in the reply, forbid a verdict, require 'Ann Tone' (`as-written:`) and forbid 'rendering of', 'variant of' and 'split'. `transcribes-in-place` asserts the router transcribed in place and read the staged page. A transcription takes no hand-off, so the brief rule (step 4) is pinned by ut_research_iv3, not here.

input.user_message: /research I uploaded page 36 of the 1880 census for the Tyler household (record ark:/61903/1:1:MC5S-GVQ) as uploads/1880-census-cunningham-p36.png. The index has her as Armtogne Tyler, and her 1923 death certificate, already in the project, names her Ann Tone Lightfoot. Transcribe line 43 and tell me how her name there compares with those.

judge_context: On line 43 the index reads Armtogne and the machine reading gives Armistead. The researcher who read the image says the machine reading is far off and the index close; the true value is withheld from you, as it is from the skill, and is not graded. The 1923 death certificate (ark:/61903/1:1:QVR7-5LJJ) writes the given name as two words, Ann Tone.

A pass: the reply shows the index reading and the machine reading side by side, says they differ, points to line 43 on the image, and reports the certificate's name as written, 'Ann Tone', without folding it into another record's spelling.
A fail: 'line 43 is clear', calling the index a misread or a poor attempt, stating a correction, or calling 'Ann Tone' a rendering, variant or split of another name.

The reply cannot know the true value: no tool or project file gives it. Reporting 'Armistead' as what the machine reading returned is required, not an error, and is never marked down. What is graded is whether the reply treats that reading as the answer, for example by calling it the name on the image or the more plausible reading.
